items.title: BREAKING: Global central bank gold purchases rose +62 tonnes YoY in Q2 2026, to 289 tonnes, the biggest quarterly addition since Q4 2024. Quarter-over-quarter, gold purchases surged +231 tonnes, or +407%. Year-to-date, central banks have acquired +345 tonnes of gold. Poland has led these purchases at +82 tonnes, bringing its total reserves to a record 632 tonnes. Uzbekistan and China followed, adding +41 tonnes and +40 tonnes, respectively, so far this year. Central banks continue to accumulate gold at a rapid pace.

items.content:
BREAKING: Global household net worth surged +7.3% YoY, to a record $570 trillion in 2025.

This was primarily driven by equities which accounted for 57% of the increase, while real estate contributed just 15%.

Since 2000, this figure has risen +338%, with an average annual increase of +5.9%.

As a result, global household net worth is now equivalent to ~380% of world GDP.

Real estate accounts for ~50% of the total, followed by equities and investment funds at ~25%, bonds and pensions at 20%, and cash deposits at 20%.

This is somewhat offset by loans, which equal ~15% of the full amount.

Among countries, US household net worth stood at $175 trillion last year, +133% above China's $75 trillion and +661% above Germany's $23 trillion.

Own assets or be left behind.

items.title: BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.1 percentage point in June, to 2.7%, the lowest since June 2022. This marks the 5th consecutive monthly decline, bringing the cumulative drop to -1.7 percentage points. This is also the 3rd-lowest monthly reading since April 2008, during the Financial Crisis. To put this into perspective, the personal savings rate averaged ~5.5% between 2014 and 2019. The only period in modern history with similarly low saving rates was 2005-2007, when the rate fluctuated between 1.4% and 3.3%. US households are struggling to save money.

items.title: China’s economy is losing momentum: China's manufacturing PMI fell -1.1 points in July, to 49.2, one of the lowest readings since 2023. This also marks the first reading below 50 since February, signaling contraction in the sector. At the same time, non-manufacturing PMI, measuring construction and services activity, declined -1.2 points, to 49.0, the lowest since December 2022. Construction PMI alone dropped 2.0 points, to 47.0 points, the lowest since the 2020 pandemic. On top of this, China’s GDP growth slowed to just +4.3% YoY in Q2 2026, the weakest expansion since Q4 2022. China’s slowdown is spreading across its economy.

items.title: The US ETF industry is seeing unprecedented growth: There have been ~390 US-listed ETF launches over the last 2 months, the largest 2-month increase on record. This figure has more than tripled since the start of 2024. As a result, more ETFs have launched over the last 2 months than during the entire first half of 2024. Of all ETFs introduced this year, 54% incorporate derivatives, and over 33% are classified as leveraged or inverse funds. Furthermore, fund issuers have already filed for more than 1,000 leveraged ETFs so far this year, pointing to another wave of launches ahead. The ETF market is expanding faster than ever.
